notes: All Azure DevOps read tools are labeled SECRET because they use the user's authenticated `connectionProvider`/token and can return non-public SaaS data from the configured organization.

UNTRUSTED is applied where the returned data includes source-controlled content, build logs, wiki/work item/PR comments, search snippets, or other multi-writer/public project content that an attacker could author.
SINK is applied to tools that store agent-supplied content or state into Azure DevOps records or trigger/update shared resources; such records may be visible in public or multi-user projects.

advsec_get_alert_details.rationale: Reads a specific Advanced Security alert through authenticated `alertApi.getAlert`. Alert details may include secret/security findings and repository-derived attacker-influenced text such as refs, paths, rules, or messages.

advsec_get_alerts.rationale: Reads Advanced Security alerts with authenticated `alertApi.getAlerts`. Alerts can include secret-alert/security details and repository-derived paths/rule data; repository-derived fields may be influenced by attacker-authored code in multi-writer repos.

core_get_identity_ids.rationale: Calls authenticated identity search (`searchIdentities`) and returns identity IDs, display names, and descriptors, which are non-public directory/account data.

core_list_project_teams.rationale: Uses the authenticated Azure DevOps connection (`connectionProvider`, `connection.getCoreApi()`) and returns teams from `coreApi.getTeams`, so it can disclose non-public organization/team membership data available to the user.

core_list_projects.rationale: Uses the authenticated Azure DevOps connection and returns projects from `coreApi.getProjects`, disclosing organization project metadata available to the user.

pipelines_artifact.rationale: Lists and downloads authenticated build artifacts. Downloaded artifact bytes are returned as base64 or written locally; artifact contents can be produced by builds from multi-writer repositories and are attacker-controllable.

pipelines_build.rationale: Reads builds, build reports, and build changes using authenticated `buildApi`. Build metadata/changes are non-public SaaS data; commits, build numbers, tags, issues, and change data can be authored or influenced by repository contributors, so returned text may be attacker-controlled in multi-writer repos.

pipelines_build_log.rationale: Reads authenticated build logs via `getBuildLogs`/`getBuildLogLines`. Log content can contain output from source-controlled build scripts or tests in multi-writer repositories, so `get_content` returns attacker-controllable text.

pipelines_definition.rationale: Uses authenticated Build/Git APIs to list pipeline definitions and revisions, exposing non-public project pipeline configuration metadata.

pipelines_run.rationale: Reads pipeline runs through authenticated `pipelinesApi.getRun`/`listRuns`, exposing non-public pipeline run metadata.

pipelines_write.rationale: Can queue pipeline runs (`runPipeline`), create pipeline definitions (`createPipeline`), and update build stages by PATCH. Agent-supplied values such as `variables`, `templateParameters`, `yamlOverride`, `name`, `folder`, and `yamlPath` are sent/stored in Azure DevOps and may be visible through public/shared projects or pipeline logs.

repo_branch.rationale: Reads repository refs with user credentials. Branch names are returned and can be created/named by contributors in multi-writer repositories.

repo_create_branch.rationale: Creates a Git ref via `gitApi.updateRefs`; agent-supplied `branchName` is stored as a repository branch name that may be public/shared. Source branch names may also be contributor-authored.

repo_file.rationale: Reads repository file contents and directory listings from authenticated Azure Repos. File content, paths, and filenames are source-controlled and can be attacker-authored in multi-writer/public repositories.

repo_pull_request.rationale: Reads pull requests and PR metadata with user credentials. PR `title`, `description`, branch names, labels, and changed-file data can be authored by contributors in multi-writer/public repositories, so returned content may be attacker-controlled.

repo_pull_request_thread.rationale: Reads PR threads/comments using authenticated `gitApi.getThreads`/`getComments`. Comment `content` and author identity fields come from PR participants and are attacker-controllable in public or multi-writer repos.

repo_pull_request_thread_write.rationale: Creates PR comment threads/replies and updates thread status. Agent-supplied `content` is posted to PR comments, an attacker-readable destination in public/shared repos. Returned thread/comment data includes comment `content` and author fields.

repo_pull_request_write.rationale: Creates/updates PRs, reviewers, labels, and votes using authenticated Git APIs. Agent-supplied PR `title`, `description`, `labels`, `mergeCommitMessage`, `bypassReason`, reviewers, and branch/PR identifiers are stored in Azure DevOps and may be visible to other users/public projects. Returned PR fields can include contributor-authored PR text.

repo_repository.rationale: Reads repositories from authenticated `gitApi.getRepositories` and returns repository metadata for the user's Azure DevOps project/organization.

repo_search_commits.rationale: Posts a commit search to Azure DevOps with the user's token and returns search results. Commit messages, authors, branch/repository names, and other result text may be authored by repository contributors.

search_code.rationale: Searches authenticated Azure DevOps code search and then fetches matching Git items with content. Source code snippets, file paths, repository metadata, and file contents are attacker-controllable in multi-writer repositories.

search_wiki.rationale: Searches Azure DevOps Wiki with the user's token and returns raw search results; wiki content, page titles, and snippets are collaborative/attacker-controllable in public or multi-writer wikis.

search_workitem.rationale: Searches authenticated work item search and returns raw results. Work item titles/descriptions/fields and snippets are authored by project contributors and may be attacker-controlled.

testplan.rationale: Reads test plans, suites, and cases via authenticated Azure DevOps REST calls. Test plan/suite/case names and details can be authored by project contributors.

testplan_show_test_results_from_build_id.rationale: Reads authenticated test results for a build. Test titles, error messages, stack traces, automated test names, and storage paths can be produced by repository tests/builds and are attacker-controllable in multi-writer repos.

testplan_test_case_write.rationale: Creates test case work items and updates test steps. Agent-supplied `title` and `steps` are stored in Azure DevOps work item/test case fields; stored/returned work item fields can be attacker-authored in shared projects.

testplan_test_plan_write.rationale: Creates a test plan with agent-supplied `name`, `iteration`, `description`, dates, and area path via authenticated `createTestPlan`; these values are stored in Azure DevOps and may be visible to shared/public projects.

testplan_test_suite_write.rationale: Creates test suites and adds test cases to suites. Agent-supplied `name` and test case IDs are stored/associated in Azure DevOps test plan records.

wiki.rationale: Reads wiki metadata and page content with the user's Azure DevOps credentials. Wiki page content, paths, and titles are collaborative documentation and may be attacker-authored; `url` is parsed and constrained to the configured organization before fetching from `connection.serverUrl`.

wiki_upsert_page.rationale: Creates or updates wiki pages via PUT; agent-supplied `content` is stored in a wiki page and may be attacker-readable in public/shared wikis. The response includes page metadata/content from the wiki service.

wit_backlog.rationale: Reads backlog levels and work items using authenticated Work API. Returned backlog/work item data may include names and work item references from multi-writer project planning data.

wit_query.rationale: Runs saved/ad-hoc work item queries with user credentials and returns query definitions/results. Query results can include work item fields authored by project contributors; WIQL results are wrapped as external content.

wit_work_item.rationale: Reads work items, comments, revisions, and iteration work items using authenticated APIs. Work item titles/descriptions/fields/comments are multi-writer project content and may be attacker-authored.

wit_work_item_attachment.rationale: Downloads authenticated work item attachment content. Attachments can be uploaded by work item participants, so returned text/base64 content is attacker-controllable; if `savePath` is provided it writes the attachment to a local relative path.

wit_work_item_comment_write.rationale: Adds or updates work item comments by POST/PATCH; agent-supplied `text` is stored in Azure DevOps comments, which may be visible to other users/public projects. The response body may include rendered/stored comment text.

wit_work_item_link_write.rationale: Creates/removes work item links and artifact links by updating work item relations. Agent-supplied URLs/artifact URIs/comments and IDs are stored in work item relations that may be shared/public. `unlink` also returns existing relation data, which may include user-authored relation comments/URLs.

wit_work_item_write.rationale: Creates/updates work items and child work items using authenticated APIs/fetch. Agent-supplied field values, update values, titles, and descriptions are stored in Azure DevOps work items that may be shared/public. Returned work item data can include user-authored fields.

work.rationale: Reads Azure DevOps work/iteration/team settings and capacity through authenticated APIs (`getWorkApi`, `getWorkItemTrackingApi`), exposing non-public project/team planning data.

work_capacity_write.rationale: Updates a team member's capacity using `updateCapacityWithIdentityRef`; agent-supplied `activities` and `daysOff` are stored in Azure DevOps team capacity records.

work_iteration_write.rationale: Creates or assigns Azure DevOps iterations via `createOrUpdateClassificationNode` and `postTeamIteration`; agent-supplied `iterations` data is written into project/team records that may be visible to other users or public projects.

value_conditions.effect: Tools are registered only when their domain is enabled. The default `all` enables every domain except `mcp-apps`, so all advertised tools in this assessment are default-enabled. Supplying a subset such as `-d core work` removes tools from other domains.

value_conditions.default: interactive outside Codespaces; azcli in Codespaces
value_conditions.effect: In PAT mode, a global fetch interceptor rewrites `Authorization: Bearer ...` to `Authorization: Basic ...`; this changes authentication mechanics but does not remove tools or labels.
